Amsterdam Temperature Anomalies, 1996–2025

Hourly KNMI station readings for Amsterdam Schiphol (station 240), aggregated to daily averages and compared against a 30‑year day‑of‑year normal. This dashboard surfaces the days that broke furthest from that normal — and the real weather events behind the biggest swings.

Key findings

Daily temperature anomaly vs. normal

Each bar is one day's average temperature, minus the typical temperature for that calendar day (based on a ±7‑day window across all 30 years). Markers mark the 12 events profiled below.

Every day, 1996–2025

Each row is a year, each column a day of the year. Color shows how far that day's average temperature sat from normal — deep red for exceptional warmth, deep blue for exceptional cold.

The events behind the anomalies

Twelve of the most extreme days in this record, matched with the news coverage of the weather event that caused them. Each mini‑chart shows hourly temperature for the surrounding nine days.

Average temperature per year

Each point is one year's average across all its daily readings. The dashed line is the linear trend across the full 30 years.

Yearly average Linear trend
Data: hourly temperature observations, Amsterdam Schiphol (KNMI station 240), Jan 1996 – Dec 2025, 262,992 hourly readings aggregated to 10,958 days. "Normal" = mean of that calendar day ± 7 days across all 30 years. Event descriptions summarize public reporting cited on each card; figures there refer to national/regional records (De Bilt, Gilze‑Rijen, etc.), which may differ slightly from this Schiphol station's own reading on the same day.
